title: How do we draw sets of parallel lines on dot paper?
description: The board draws flat, upright and leaning sets of parallel segments on dot paper. Each leaning set repeats the same steps from different dots, so the gap stays the same.
teaching_notes: One idea: segments that repeat the same steps from different dots keep the same gap, so they are parallel. Their lengths may differ.

source: Figure it Out (parallel and perpendicular lines), Q3
video_script.why: The child has seen that parallel lines keep the same gap and now draws sets of parallel lines.
video_script.substitution: Draw sets of segments that run the same way, the same way as the example in the book, by repeating the same steps from different dots.
video_script.anchor: A blank dot paper with rows and columns of dots.
video_script.payoff_line: Draw flat sets, upright sets and leaning sets, and repeat the same steps for each leaning set.

final_answer.value: Sets of flat lines, upright lines and leaning lines that repeat the same steps, such as 1 across and 1 up, or 2 across and 1 up
final_answer.spoken: sets of flat lines, upright lines and leaning lines that repeat the same steps, such as one across and one up, or two across and one up

hold_back: Sets of flat lines, upright lines and leaning lines that repeat the same steps, such as 1 across and 1 up, or 2 across and 1 up
maths_rules: flat segments in different rows are parallel and may have different lengths
upright segments in different columns are parallel
leaning segments that start at different dots and repeat the same steps, for example 1 across and 1 up, or 2 across and 1 up, are parallel
the same steps keep the same gap, so the lines are parallel
the endpoints of every segment must be dots
video_script.design: One blank dot paper stays on the stage. Each set is drawn in its own colour, and the steps are written beside each leaning set.
